_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with insomnia, characterized by difficulties with sleep onset and/or sleep maintenance

pivotal_trials.nct: 0295820 (as reported in the review's controlled-studies table for Study E2006-G000-303 Core Period 1; NCT number appears truncated/OCR-altered in the source)
pivotal_trials.design: 12-month, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study of lemborexant 5 mg or 10 mg nightly
pivotal_trials.population: Adults age >=18 years with DSM-5 insomnia disorder, no current other sleep disorders, ISI >=15
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Mean change from baseline to end of treatment at 6 months in subjective sleep onset latency (sSOL)
pivotal_trials.n: 971 randomized: LEM5 n=316, LEM10 n=315, PBO n=318 (ITT)
pivotal_trials.result: Both doses superior to placebo on sSOL at Month 6: LSGM active/placebo ratio 0.73 (95% CI 0.64, 0.84) for LEM5 and 0.70 (95% CI 0.61, 0.81) for LEM10, both p<0.001

nct_ctgov.title: Long-term Study of Lemborexant in Insomnia Disorder (SUNRISE 2)

pivotal_trials.design: Global, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, active-comparator (zolpidem ER) parallel-group study of lemborexant 5 mg and 10 mg for 30 nights
pivotal_trials.population: Males >=65 years and females >=55 years with DSM-5 insomnia disorder, ISI >=13
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Mean change in latency to persistent sleep (LPS) from baseline to end of treatment (day 29/30) measured by overnight polysomnography
pivotal_trials.n: 1006 randomized: LEM5 n=266, LEM10 n=269, ZOL n=263, PBO n=208
pivotal_trials.result: Both doses superior to placebo on LPS at day 29/30: LSGM active/placebo ratio 0.77 (95% CI 0.67, 0.89) for LEM5 and 0.72 (95% CI 0.63, 0.83) for LEM10, both p<0.001

key_safety: Most common adverse reaction was somnolence (10% for DAYVIGO 10 mg, 7% for 5 mg, 1% for placebo). Combined somnolence/fatigue occurred in 9.6% (10 mg), 6.9% (5 mg) vs 1.3% placebo. Warnings include CNS depressant effects/daytime impairment, sleep paralysis/hallucinations/cataplexy-like symptoms, complex sleep behaviors, and worsening depression/suicidal ideation.
target_moa: Orexin receptor antagonist; competitive antagonist at OX1R and OX2R (higher affinity for OX2R) that blocks binding of the wake-promoting neuropeptides orexin A and orexin B to suppress wake drive

rems.type: No safety issues necessitating a REMS were identified.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the Division did not identify questions requiring discussion by the Psychopharmacologic Drugs Advisory Committee or the Drug Safety and Risk Management Advisory Committee.

description.text: Updated Warnings and Precautions and Use in Specific Populations to reflect respiratory safety results in OSA and COPD patients (PMR 3753-1 fulfillment), not a new indication

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides the results of postmarketing study requirement (PMR 3753-1) listed in the approval letter dated December 20, 2019. It further proposes revisions to Section 5 *Warnings and Precautions*, and Section 8 *Use in Specific Populations* of the USPI to reflect the results of this PMR.

summary.text: DAYVIGO (lemborexant) was submitted as a standard-review NDA (received 12/27/2018) for adults with insomnia and approved 12/20/2019 within the first review cycle. No accelerated approval, breakthrough, fast track, orphan, or priority-review designations were applied; FDA intended to recommend scheduling under the Controlled Substances Act, so the approval date was tied to DEA scheduling.

citations.quote: This new drug application provides for the use of Dayvigo (lemborexant) tablets for the treatment of adult patients with insomnia, characterized by difficulties with sleep onset and/or sleep maintenance.

You were previously informed that FDA intends to recommend scheduling of Dayvigo under the Controlled Substances Act (CSA). The scheduling of this product in accordance with the CSA (21 U.S.C. 811) is not yet complete as of the date of this letter.
